arxiv-2305-13656.creator: Zexi Huang, Mert Kosan, Arlei Silva, Ambuj Singh
arxiv-2305-13656.description: Abstract . Link prediction, which consists of predicting edges based on graph features, is a fundamental task in many graph applications. As for several related problems, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), which are based on an attribute-centric message-passing paradigm, have become the predominant framework for link prediction. GNNs have consistently outperformed traditional topology-based heuristics, but what contributes to their performance?

arxiv-2502-08859.title: EnigmaEval : A Benchmark of Long Multimodal Reasoning Challenges
arxiv-2502-08859.creator: Clinton J. Wang, Dean Lee, Cristina Menghini, Johannes Mols, Jack Doughty, Adam Khoja, Jayson Lynch, Sean Hendryx, Summer Yue, Dan Hendrycks
arxiv-2502-08859.description: Abstract As language models master existing reasoning benchmarks, we need new challenges to evaluate their cognitive frontiers. Puzzle-solving events are rich repositories of challenging multimodal problems that test a wide range of advanced reasoning and knowledge capabilities, making them a unique testbed for evaluating frontier language models.

arxiv-2506-24008.title: Spatial QUBO: Convolutional Formulation of Large-Scale Binary Optimization with Dense Interactions
arxiv-2506-24008.creator: Hiroshi Yamashita, Hideyuki Suzuki
arxiv-2506-24008.description: Abstract The spatial photonic Ising machine (SPIM) is a promising optical hardware solver for large-scale combinatorial optimization problems with dense interactions. As the SPIM can represent Ising problems with rank-one coupling matrices, multiplexed versions have been proposed to enhance the applicability to higher-rank interactions.

arxiv-2509-04966.title: Neuro-Spectral Architectures for Causal Physics-Informed Networks
arxiv-2509-04966.creator: Arthur Bizzi, Leonardo Moreira, Márcio Macedo, Leonardo Mendonça, Christian Oliveira, Vitor Balestro, Lucas Fernandez, Daniel Yukimura, Pavel Petrov, João M. Pereira, Tiago Novello, Lucas Nissenbaum
arxiv-2509-04966.description: Abstract Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a powerful neural framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs). However, standard MLP-based PINNs often fail to converge when dealing with complex initial-value problems, leading to solutions that violate causality and suffer from a spectral bias towards low-frequency components.

arxiv-2601-23229.title: Strongly Polynomial Time Complexity of Policy Iteration for L ∞ L_{\infty} Robust MDPs
arxiv-2601-23229.creator: Ali Asadi, Krishnendu Chatterjee, Ehsan Goharshady, Mehrdad Karrabi, Alipasha Montaseri, Carlo Pagano
arxiv-2601-23229.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Ali Asadi, Krishnendu Chatterjee, Ehsan Goharshady, Mehrdad Karrabi, Alipasha Montaseri, Carlo Pagano. Markov decision processes (MDPs) are a fundamental model in sequential decision making. Robust MDPs (RMDPs) extend this framework by allowing uncertainty in transition probabilities and optimizing against the worst-case realization of that uncertainty. In particular, ( s , a ) (s,a) -rectangular RMDPs with L ∞ L_{\infty} uncertainty sets form a fundamental and expressive model: they subsume classical MDPs and turn-based stochastic games. We consider this model with discounted payoffs.

pmc-11483760.title: Health Risk Assessment of Heavy Metals in Lettuce and Spring Onion on Human Health in Kumasi, Ghana
pmc-11483760.creator: Prince Owusu Adoma, Afia Sakyiwaa Amponsah, Kwarteng Twumasi Ankrah, Francis Acquah, Hubert Amu, Richard Osei Agjei, Ruby Hanson
pmc-11483760.description: Introduction:The demand and consumption of vegetables are significantly increasing worldwide, which has resulted in urban farming on anthropogenic sites. This study assessed the concentrations of some selected heavy metals in lettuce and spring onion in line with the WHO/FAO required standard and its implications on human health.Methods:The study was carried out in Kumasi, within moist semi-deciduous forest vegetation, Ghana.

pmc-11531906.title: Current recycling innovations to utilize e-waste in sustainable green metal manufacturing
pmc-11531906.creator: Rumana Hossain, Veena Sahajwalla
pmc-11531906.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The ever-increasing market demand and the rapid uptake of the technologies of electronics create an unavoidable generation of high-volume electronic waste (e-waste). E-waste is embedded with valuable metals, alloys, precious metals and rare earth elements. A substantial portion of e-waste ends up in landfills and is incinerated due to its complex multi-material structure, creating loss of resources and often leading to environmental contamination from the release of landfill leachates and combustion gases.

pmc-11621362.title: Attenuation of skin injury by a MARCO targeting PLGA nanoparticle
pmc-11621362.creator: Ummiye V Onay, Dan Xu, Dauren Biyashev, Spencer T Evans, Michael M Demczuk, Tobias Neef, Joseph R Podojil, Sara Beddow, Nathan C Gianneschi, I Caroline Le Poole, Stephen D Miller, Kurt Q Lu
pmc-11621362.description: Cutaneous exposure to the DNA alkylating class of chemotherapeutic agents including nitrogen mustard (NM) leads to both skin injury and systemic inflammation. Circulating myeloid subsets recruited to the skin act to further exacerbate local tissue damage while interfering with the wound healing process.

pmc-11629865.title: Role of Autophagy in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: The Metabolic Clash
pmc-11629865.creator: Yousef Abud Alanazi, Haydar M. Al‐kuraishy, Ali I. Al‐Gareeb, Athanasios Alexiou, Marios Papadakis, Mostafa M. Bahaa, Walaa A. Negm, Faisal Holil AlAnazi, Mohammed Alrouji, Gaber El‐Saber Batiha
pmc-11629865.description: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is developed due to the development of insulin resistance (IR) and pancreatic β cell dysfunction with subsequent hyperglycaemia. Hyperglycaemia‐induced oxidative stress and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress enhances inflammatory disorders, leading to further pancreatic β cell dysfunction. These changes trigger autophagy activation, which recycles cytoplasmic components and injured organelles.

pmc-11660659.title: Impact of Chronic Intermittent Hypoxia on Cognitive Function and Hippocampal Neurons in Mice: A Study of Inflammatory and Oxidative Stress Pathways
pmc-11660659.creator: Kai Zhang, Dandi Ma, Yunxiao Wu, Zhifei Xu
pmc-11660659.description: PurposeChronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) is considered one of the main pathophysiological mechanisms of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). CIH can further lead to cognitive dysfunction by inducing processes such as neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. The hippocampus is primarily associated with cognitive functions such as learning and memory.

pmc-12597844.title: Unraveling the Ecological Mechanisms Influencing the Structure and Composition of Lung Cancer Microbiomes
pmc-12597844.creator: Jiandong Mei, Lianwei Li, Zhanshan Sam Ma
pmc-12597844.description: This study investigates the ecological mechanisms governing the structure and composition of lung microbiome communities within tumor tissue from lung cancer patients. While this field has attracted increasing research attention, the ecological and etiological mechanisms driving microbial community assembly in this environment remain poorly characterized. To address this gap, we applied Sloan’s near neutral model, Ning et al.

pmc-12820720.title: Development and Comparability of Internalizing and Externalizing Symptom Spectra From Adolescence to Young Adulthood
pmc-12820720.creator: Vera Birgel, Michael Rapp, Mira Tschorn, Heike Hölling, Caroline Cohrdes
pmc-12820720.description: ObjectivesThis study examines the continuity and comparability of internalizing and externalizing symptom spectra from adolescence to young adulthood, addressing measurement challenges across developmental stages. Leveraging the Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP) framework, it explores whether symptom spectra in adolescence predict corresponding symptoms in young adulthood.

pmc-13451453.title: Frontotemporal dementia with right temporal predominance: a clinical comparison with left-predominant FTD
pmc-13451453.creator: Jennifer C Thompson, Christopher Kobylecki, Matthew Jones, Jessica Haigh, Matthew Larbey, Tobias C Langheinrich, Rachel Thomasson, Anna M T Richardson, Julie S Snowden
pmc-13451453.description: BackgroundThe right-temporal variant of frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is well characterised. Whether it should be considered a distinct clinical entity, separate from other syndromes of FTD, remains an open question. The study addressed the issue through a retrospective comparison of clinical characteristics of patients with predominant atrophy in right or left anterior temporal lobe (R-ATL vs. L-ATL).

pmc-13659666.title: Durability of a physician-modified endograft constructed using the Terumo Aortic TREO device: A postmortem evaluation
pmc-13659666.creator: Nicolas A. Stafforini, Sara L. Zettervall, Allison Larimore, Benjamin W. Starnes
pmc-13659666.description: Fenestrated endovascular repair using physician-modified endografts has become an important treatment option for complex abdominal aortic aneurysms, although long-term graft durability data remain limited. We present a unique postmortem evaluation of a physician-modified endograft implanted for a juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm as part of an Investigational Device Exemption trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT01538056).
